title: Buffy the Vampire Slayer
subtitle: Sunnydale becomes a place to fight through
summary: Buffy the Vampire Slayer is The Collective's action-adventure game, first released for Xbox on 19 August 2002. Set during the television series' third season, it follows Buffy and her friends as they confront an ancient being threatening the world. Sunnydale provides the places and familiar faces around a campaign built around physical combat. Buffy moves through thirteen levels, fighting supernatural enemies, crossing obstacles and solving occasional environmental puzzles. body: Buffy the Vampire Slayer is The Collective's action-adventure game, first released for Xbox on 19 August 2002. Set during the television series' third season, it follows Buffy and her friends as they confront an ancient being threatening the world. Sunnydale provides the places and familiar faces around a campaign built around physical combat. Buffy moves through thirteen levels, fighting supernatural enemies, crossing obstacles and solving occasional environmental puzzles. Visits to the school library connect those encounters to the supporting cast, allowing the player to regroup and prepare for the next excursion.

Punches, kicks and throws can be combined while targeting a particular enemy or striking several opponents nearby. Objects found around Sunnydale become weapons, but repeated use wears them down. A bat or shovel can break into a smaller implement before finally becoming unusable, making the surroundings part of the fight. Crossbows and holy water offer other responses at a distance. The player therefore has to read what is available as well as the creature approaching. The immediate weapon may work differently a few blows later, changing the next choice within the same confrontation.

Christopher Golden and Thomas Sniegoski, already familiar with the Buffy universe through their novels, wrote the story. The Collective developed its Slayer Engine for the project after moving production from earlier planned platforms to Xbox. Reviews praised the combat and the connection to the television series. The game makes its source material useful through action: Buffy's strength, improvised weapons and recurring visits to her friends all become things the player experiences. Its appeal comes from joining the show's familiar setting to a fighting system capable of supporting a complete console adventure.
